Yes. The most direct match is ruleXplain, which uses LLMs to learn symbolic causal rules from multivariate time series. It defines a constrained rule language with temporal operators and delay semantics, generates counterfactual trajectories from a simulator, and has the LLM produce verifiable causal rules with closed-loop refinement for consistency and semantic validity [1]. This is specifically about causal explanations in time series, not just forecasting [1].

Related but different papers cover adjacent ideas. Large Causal Models target temporal causal discovery with pre-trained neural architectures rather than explicit symbolic rules [4]. CauScientist uses LLMs to propose and refine causal graphs with statistical verification, but the abstract does not focus on time-series rule extraction [6]. For logical-rule-constrained LLM reasoning more generally, PCRLLM and LOVER impose stepwise logical constraints or logical-rule regularization, but they are not about time-series causality in their abstracts [9, 10].
